obligations.source_text: this verb inverts the repo's content-retention rule and must say so out loud: members drops content at aggregation (jlab/members/aggregate.py:38-58,:119-122 keep only len() and a bool) and links keeps the URL and nothing else (jlab/links/extract.py:245-258) — a regex search over message bodies cannot exist without surfacing the body text itself, so retention has to be a stated, bounded decision rather than an accident

obligations.behavior: results on stdout, diagnostics on stderr, --json everywhere, errors as error:/hint: or {code,message,remediation} with no traceback — enforced by 'teken cli doctor . --strict' passing unchanged in CI
obligations.source_text: the agent-first contracts hold unchanged: results to stdout and diagnostics to stderr via jlab/cli/_output.py:17-53, --json on every command, and failures as CliError(EXIT_USER_ERROR=1) — a malformed --grep pattern is user input, matching the code-1 precedent at jlab/cli/_discord.py:123-134 and _commands/discord.py:216-229, not an environment error

obligations.seam: jlab discord doctor and the cache connection
obligations.behavior: an absent or unreachable jlab-mongodb reports a code-2 environment error with an actionable hint; it never yields a silent empty result that reads as 'no matches'
obligations.source_text: standing up jlab-mongodb is part of this feature's cost, not a free precondition: the earlier rationale for MongoDB was that an instance already existed so none had to be raised, and choosing a dedicated instance reverses that — the feature now owns a container to run, a port to pick, and an operator setup step to document, plus a doctor check that reports clearly when the instance is absent or unreachable

obligations.behavior: a caller passing no new flag gets byte-identical output to today, so lifting the 100 bound is additive and cannot regress an existing user or script
obligations.source_text: the 100-message ceiling is jlab's own hardcoded bound, not a Discord limit: jlab/cli/_discord.py:422 validates 'if not 1 <= limit <= 100' and line 431 issues a single unwindowed channel.history(limit=limit) — lifting the ceiling means replacing that one call, not working around an API cap

obligations.behavior: coverage widens only after the messages in that span are durably written, and concurrent fetches against the same channel are serialised — an interrupted or interleaved run leaves coverage narrower than reality, never wider
obligations.source_text: nothing serialises two fetches against the same channel: the frame's only concurrency control is the asyncio semaphore bounding per-channel fan-out inside one invocation, but the cache is now shared state across invocations, and this agent runs in a mesh where more than one session can invoke the CLI — two overlapping fetches can interleave writes and leave a coverage record claiming a span neither actually completed, which is the same silent over-claim as the disjoint-interval gap but arriving by a different route

obligations.seam: regex matching over the cached corpus
obligations.behavior: a pathological pattern terminates within a declared bound and reports that it was bounded; it never hangs and never returns an empty result that reads as 'no matches'
obligations.source_text: a caller-supplied regex over a large corpus is an availability hazard with no guard: the compile-time validation catches malformed patterns, but a well-formed pattern with catastrophic backtracking will hang, and Python's re offers no timeout — the existing verbs never took a pattern from the user, so this risk is new with this feature

obligations.behavior: the bind address and the internal-network assumption it rests on are written down beside the setup command, so a deployment onto a less trusted network is a visible change of posture
obligations.source_text: jlab-mongodb's network posture is a stated, approved decision rather than an oversight: both mongo containers measured on this machine bind 0.0.0.0 (qq-mongodb 27017, eidetic-mongo 27018), and jlab-mongodb following that pattern is accepted because the exposure is confined to an internal network — what this claim requires is that the posture is written down as a choice, so a later move to a less trusted network is recognised as changing it

obligations.behavior: a purge by author id removes that author's messages from the cache and from derived reports, verified by a test that fetches, purges, then searches and finds nothing for that author
obligations.source_text: a per-user deletion mechanism is required, not optional: Discord's Developer Terms require API Data to be deleted when the applicable user requests deletion, when Discord requests deletion, or when retaining it is no longer necessary for the stated functionality — so the cache needs a way to purge one author's content, a way to honour a platform request, and a retention bound tied to what the feature actually needs

obligations.behavior: encryption at rest is on and doctor reports it as measured rather than assumed
obligations.source_text: the cache must be encrypted at rest: Discord's Developer Terms require it specifically, and this is the first jlab surface that stores API Data at all — the members path kept only derived integers and the links path only URLs, so no existing jlab store had to meet this bar

obligations.seam: the published privacy policy and its Developer Portal link
obligations.behavior: the policy describes collection, storage, retention, sharing and deletion for this cache specifically, and the Portal link resolves to it
obligations.source_text: the agent needs a privacy policy describing collection, storage, retention, sharing and deletion, with an up-to-date link in the Discord Developer Portal; this is satisfiable by a static Markdown or GitHub page and does not make the software a web service

obligations.seam: coverage arithmetic over a window with an interior gap
obligations.behavior: a search whose requested window is only partially covered reports the uncovered spans rather than returning the covered subset as if it were complete; a test fetches two disjoint spans and asserts the gap between them is named, not silently swallowed
obligations.source_text: a single oldest/newest coverage pair cannot represent disjoint fetches and will silently over-claim: the recorded instruction on the incremental-fetch requirement says to track 'oldest and newest message id or timestamp fetched', but fetching September and later fetching January produces two disjoint spans that a single pair reports as one continuous window — a subsequent search would then answer from a cache it believes complete while months in the middle were never downloaded, defeating the gap-only obligation rather than fulfilling it

obligations.behavior: the cache converges to Discord's current state — edits applied, deletions removed, newly-private channels purged — using only the sweep, with no event listener running; a test drives a full reconciliation cycle without any gateway connection
obligations.source_text: events cannot replace the periodic sweep, only reduce its load: a gateway delivers MESSAGE_DELETE and MESSAGE_UPDATE only to a client that is connected when they happen, so anything occurring while the daemon is down, restarting, or disconnected is lost with no backfill — and Discord does not replay them — which means the daily reconciliation stays the correctness backstop and events become a latency improvement on top of it

obligations.behavior: the sweep covers every cached channel and window it is responsible for; a rate-limit encounter delays it rather than silently narrowing what it reconciles, and an incomplete sweep reports itself as incomplete
obligations.source_text: the cost of re-reading a window to detect deletions is accepted and is not a reason to weaken the sweep: re-reading is a loop of code and cheap, while failing to respect a member's privacy is expensive — so the sweep's frequency and completeness are set by the privacy obligation, never trimmed to save requests

obligations.seam: discord read against an uncovered window
obligations.behavior: a read whose window the cache does not cover reports the gap and points at --refresh, and never returns an empty result that a caller would read as 'this channel had no messages' — supersedes o11, whose unconditional byte-identical promise no longer holds; o11 should be rejected
obligations.source_text: the read-compatibility promise is restated, not abandoned: read serves from the Mongo cache with --refresh forcing a live re-read, so 'byte-identical to today for a caller passing no new flag' holds once the channel's window is covered, and the cold-cache case — a channel never fetched — must announce that the window is uncovered rather than returning an empty result that reads as 'no messages'

obligations.behavior: --refresh is the only path by which read contacts Discord; without it read is a pure cache query, so a caller can tell from the command alone whether the network was touched
obligations.source_text: discord read serves from the Mongo cache, which the daily sweep keeps current, and gains a --refresh flag that forces a re-read from Discord when something may have been added or changed — so the cache is the default source of truth for read and the live path becomes explicit rather than implicit
